⑤ 法庭上是否实际使用“法律公报”（XML 格式）？

使用的是“原始 PDF 格式的公报”。
我们正在征求知识产权专业人士（尤其是专利专家）的意见！
2022 年 1 月 12 日及之后的公报

日本特许厅明确指出，“法律公报由公报发布网站提供，格式为XML”。此处的“XML 格式”指的是以下文档首页所示的格式。

https://t.co/bHC0RUmH1C

此外，日本特许厅于2022年1月11日之前发布的“PDF公报”已停止发行。

此前，这些已停止发行的PDF公报一直被视为“正版公报”。

自2022年1月12日起，包括INPIT在内的许多私人供应商（企业）使用各自的方法制作了PDF公报，并以“原版PDF公报”和“原版文本展示”的名义进行传播。

此外，INPIT表示：“我们无意将J-PlatPat提供的PDF文件作为‘标准’，我们相信私人企业提供的PDF文件也会被广泛传播。”

因此，“真正的专利公报”仅指专利局公报发布网站提供的“XML格式”文件，而INPIT和私营企业制作的“原始PDF公报”和“原始文本展示”不能被视为“法定公报”。

专利局似乎将“XML格式”文件称为“专利公报”。

它似乎还区分了企业制作的“原始PDF公报”和“专利信息”。

基于此，我想探讨一下法院的审理情况。

本案涉及“令和5年（和）第70102号”（专利侵权禁令及赔偿申请）（专利号：6995229），原告：李信民。

首先，以下是专利局公报发布网站上的专利号为6995229的“法定公报”（XML格式）。

https://t.co/Gntry3XaZj

接下来，这里是INPIT的J-PlatPat下载的“原始PDF出版物”和“原始文本出版物”。

https://t.co/5i6VhOa1T2

https://t.co/mmDyiHzPog

现在，进入正题。

我们将以“令和5年（和）第70102号”（专利号6995229）为例进行解释。

https://t.co/7ZQxp2DAPg

在第4页第18行及之后，“专利权利要求”部分写道：“权利要求4的发明（本发明）如下。”[权利要求4] 除红茶外的干燥半发酵茶叶，其特征在于具有以下三个特性：

(1) 去梗茶叶中多酚的重量占茶叶干重的18%或以下；

(2) 去梗茶叶中EGCG和ECG的总重量占茶叶干重的2%或以下；

(3) 去梗茶叶中儿茶素总量占茶叶干重的7%或以下；

[权利要求4] 的措辞是什么？

它与从INPIT的J-PlatPat下载的“原始PDF出版物”和“原始文本显示”中的“权利要求4”部分完全相同。

[权利要求4] 的文本来自哪里？

首先，我认为[权利要求4] 部分是原告（李新民）附在起诉状中的。

或者它是法院独立获得的？（这种可能性不大。）

此外，第20-23页指出“经查，涉案说明书包含以下陈述”，并且与上述类似，列出了看似来自“专有PDF出版物”和“专有文本显示”的内容。我认为这部分也是原告（李新民）附在起诉状中的。

日本专利局明确指出，“法定出版物由出版物发布网站提供，格式为XML。”

为什么法院不考虑“XML格式”的“法律出版物”？

法院是否仅仅接受原告提交的“专有PDF出版物”或“专有文本显示”并以此为依据作出判决？

我认为，依赖原告提交的“专有PDF出版物”和“专有文本显示”的论点完全没有意义。

“专用PDF公报”和“专用文本显示”与日本专利局先前发布的“PDF公报”截然不同，它们只能被视为“参考资料”。

（日本語原文）

くた・れAI 。AI依存症になるな ! AIを恋人にするな ！　AIを使うな、自分で考えて文章を書け ! !

⑤「法令上の公報」（XML形式）は、裁判所で実際に使われているのでしょうか？

「独自pdf公報」が使われていました。

知財関係者（特に、特許担当者）のコメントを求む ! !

2022年１月１２日以降の公報

特許庁は、「法令上の公報は、公報発行サイトから提供されるものであって、XML形式のものを指します。」と明言しています。　 そして、「ＸＭＬ形式」とは、以下の資料のフロントページにあるようなものです。

https://t.co/bHC0RUmH1C   

また、2022年１月１１日以前に特許庁より発行されていた「PDF公報」は、廃止されました。

従来は、この廃止されたPDF公報が「真正な公報」とみなされてきたと思います。

2022年１月１２日以降は、INPITをはじめ、多くの民間のベンダー（事業者）が独自の手法により作成したものが、「独自PDF公報」及び「独自テキスト表示」として流通しています。

加えて、INPITは「J-PlatPatから提供されるPDFを「標準」とする意図はなく、民間事業者が提供するPDFも流通すると考えております。」、と回答しています。

従って、「真正な特許公報」とは、特許庁の公報発行サイトから提供される「XML形式」のみのもので、INPITや各民間事業者の作成した「独自PDF公報」及び「独自テキスト表示」は「法令上の公報」とはいえないことになります。

特許庁では、「XML形式」のものを「特許公報」と呼んでいるようです。

そして、業者が作成した「独自PDF公報」のものを「特許情報」と呼んで区別しているようです。

このことを前提に、裁判所で行われている事象を検証してみたいと思います。

「令和５年（ワ）第７０１０２号」（特許権侵害差止及び特許権侵害賠償請求事件）（特許第６９９５２２９号）原告：李新敏、についてです。

先ずは、特許庁の公報発行サイトから、特許第６９９５２２９号の「XML形式」での「法令上の公報」です。

https://t.co/Gntry3XaZj   

次に、INPIT のJ-PlatPatよりダウンロードした「独自PDF公報」と「独自テキスト公報」です。

https://t.co/5i6VhOa1T2   

https://t.co/mmDyiHzPog

そして、本題です。

「令和５年（ワ）第７０１０２号」（特許第６９９５２２９号）にて説明します。

https://t.co/7ZQxp2DAPg   

４ページ目の１８行目以下に、「本権特許に係わる特許請求の範囲」として、「請求項４の発明（本発明）に係わる記載は、次のとおりである。」として、   【請求項４】紅茶を除く、乾燥した半発酵茶において、下記三つの特性を有することを特徴とする半発酵茶葉。

(1)茎が取り除かれた前記茶葉に含有されるポリフェノールの重量が当該茶葉の乾燥重量の１８重量％以下である特性；
(2)茎が取り除かれた前記茶葉に含有されるＥＧＣＧとＥＣＧの合計重量が当該茶葉の乾燥重量の２重量％以下である特性；
(3)茎が取り除かれた前記茶葉に含有される総カテキンの重量が当該茶葉の乾燥重量の７重量％以下である特性；
この【請求項4】の文面は、何でしょうか？

INPIT のJ-PlatPatよりダウンロードした「独自PDF公報」及び「独自テキスト表示」のうち、「請求項4」の部分と全く同一です。

この【請求項4】の文面は、どこから持ってきたものでしょうか？

先ず、考えられることは、この【請求項４】の部分は、原告（李新敏）が、訴状に添付したものと思います。

または、裁判所が独自に入手したものでしょうか？（これは考えられません）。

更に、２０ページ〜２３ページに「本件明細書には、以下の記載があることが認められる」として、上記と同様、「独自PDF公報」及び「独自テキスト表示」からのものと思われるものが記載されています。

これもまた、原告（李新敏）が、訴状に添付したものと思います。

特許庁は、「法令上の公報は、公報発行サイトから提供されるものであって、XML形式のものを指します。」と明言しています。

裁判所は、何故に、「法令上の公報」である「XML形式」のものを対象にしないのでしょうか？

原告が提示した「独自PDF公報」、または「独自テキスト表示」のものを鵜呑みにして、これに基づいて判断をしているのでしょうか？

原告が提示した「独自PDF公報」及び「独自テキスト表示」のものに依存した議論は、全く無意味なものと考えます。

「独自PDF公報」及び「独自テキスト表示」は、従来の特許庁が発行していた「PDF公報」とは、似ても似つかない、単なる「参考資料」としか言えないものと思います。

（井号）

items.summary:
SoftBank fixed all 10,500 security holes it found. then OpenAI's top AI looked again and found 35,000 more

in the last 5 months there have been over 45,000 security holes found in SoftBank's own systems. not in a decade. not in a year. in 5 months

any ONE of these would normally be the biggest story of the year

700 systems: built by SoftBank itself, scanned by AI in june. 10,500 holes found. every one patched over about 3 months

GPT-6 Astra: OpenAI's top model checked them again. 35,000 new holes. more than 3 times the first count

IDC Frontier: SoftBank's own cloud company, hit by ransomware about a month ago. 7 minutes from alarm to damage

495 customers: companies and local governments hit by that one attack. their servers stopped and would not restart

open source: the door the attackers used. public code nobody scanned. the CEO ordered it checked early. teams put it off

the scouting: attackers now probe SoftBank's systems 600 to 700 million times a month. double last year

attack AI: models built for hacking showed up in may and june. open versions anyone can download came out in july. new ones every week

and that's not even half the list

attackers are using AI now. attacks surged after july. too fast for human hands alone

SoftBank's CEO Junichi Miyakawa is saying every new AI model finds holes the last one missed. next week's model could find more. his words at yesterday's earnings briefing: "honestly, we're completely exhausted"

if your company runs its own software, open-source code, or cloud servers you are potentially affected

scan the open-source parts too. patch every hole you find. scan again with every new model. cut the connection first, ask questions after

this is not a normal year on the internet. this is something different

SoftBank is still patching the 35,000. follow so you see the next count first

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

items.title: Live online certificate brings AI expertise to finance professionals | Cornell Chronicle
items.summary: That philosophy is reflected in the curriculum, which progresses from AI foundations and tools to financial use cases, responsible AI, industry applications and leadership. Participants examine applications including investment research, credit risk, fraud detection, compliance, client engagement and operational efficiency, while also considering issues such as hallucinations, data security, regulation and governance. items.title: Google AI policy forces decision for San Diego schools – NBC 7 San Diego
items.summary:
As districts consider their options, students are already seeing artificial intelligence become a more common part of everyday learning.

“I feel like I see a lot of people using AI now,” said Delilah Ortiz, a student at El Camino High School.

Some students believe the focus should be on establishing guidelines for AI use rather than banning the technology entirely. [...] San Diego County school districts face a January deadline to decide whether to opt in to Google's artificial intelligence features or lose access to the company's search engine, forcing educators to weigh the benefits of AI against concerns about student access to the technology. [...] Google plans to disable a range of AI-powered features, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search in January to give school districts more control over the technology students can access. However, districts that want to continue using Google Search will have to opt in to the AI features.

items.title: Climate technology is already changing lives. Why isn’t it reaching more people? | UNEP - UN Environment Programme
items.summary:
Many developing countries still lack the technical expertise, institutional capacity and financial resources to identify and deploy technologies suited for the problems they want to tackle. On the other hand, technology cannot simply be transferred from one country to another and expected to work the same way. Instead, every solution must respond to local challenges, resources and priorities. [...] But technological advancement alone is not enough. For climate technology to grow and deliver, favorable policies and investment are absolutely key. Expanding these solutions requires infrastructure, training, institutional capacity and long-term maintenance. Without adequate financing, promising innovations risk remaining isolated projects instead of developing into widely available tools for climate resilience. [...] The Climate Technology Centre and Network is the implementation arm of the Technology Mechanism of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, hosted by the United Nations Environment Programme. It promotes the accelerated transfer of environmentally sound technologies for low-carbon and climate-resilient development at the request of developing countries, drawing on a global Network of over 1,000 member organizations across 165 countries.

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
```python
def fibonacci(n: int) -> int:
    """
    Tính số Fibonacci thứ n (n >= 0) bằng cách dùng đệ quy.

    Fibonacci(0) = 0
    Fibonacci(1) = 1
    Fibonacci(n) = Fibonacci(n-1) + Fibonacci(n-2)  (n >= 2)

    Parameters
    ----------
    n : int
        Chỉ số của dãy Fibonacci cần tính (không âm).

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Giá trị của Fibonacci thứ n.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Nếu n < 0.
    """
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("n phải là số nguyên không âm")
    if n <= 1:
        return n
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)
```

Bạn có thể gọi hàm này như sau:

```python
print(fibonacci(10))  # In ra 55
```

Lưu ý: Đệ quy thuần túy có độ phức tạp thời gian lũy thừa (O(2^n)), vì vậy cho các giá trị `n` lớn, bạn nên dùng phương pháp động (memoization) hoặc vòng lặp để tránh lặp lại tính toán.

items.summary: The promise of AI is that it gives people more power to shape their own futures. Building more computing infrastructure capacity in the United States can help lower the cost of delivering AI, put these tools in more people’s hands, and ensure America stays at the forefront of the technology. items.title: OpenAI kicks off charm offensive to change voters' view of data centers | Reuters
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

OpenAI said it will no longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites, although ​proprietary information would still be under wraps. It will also give residents access to construction plans ⁠and their potential effect on traffic, noise and lighting.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
